pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. GFL Environmental Inc. changed perimeter on September 1, 2026. SECURE was bought for about CAD 5,414.1 million, of which CAD 4,334.8 million was shares and CAD 1,079.3 million cash, but only one month of SECURE earnings is in the Q3 2026 statements. Reported leverage measures therefore carry the full debt and assumed liabilities against a partial earnings base. [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]

2. Leverage depends on management estimates. Net Leverage of 3.8x divides CAD 11,399.9 million of net debt by Run-Rate EBITDA of CAD 2,988.0 million, of which CAD 730.9 million (about a quarter) is management adjustment; on trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 2,257.1 million the same net debt is 5.05x. The covenant ceiling is 5.00x for four fiscal quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom cannot be measured. Management guides to Net Leverage "in the mid 3s" by the end of 2026, a forward claim. [CP-1 calculations]

3. Operating performance is solid by management's account. Revenue grew 27.2% in Q3 2026, Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.8%, and the quarterly Adjusted EBITDA sequence of CAD 478.5, 591.2 and 678.7 million shows growth through the year, with core pricing near 6% stated by management. The reported margin was 31.5% against 31.6% a year earlier, so margin expansion exists only in management's underlying measure, which excludes M&A and diesel effects. [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]

4. Cash generation is weaker than the management free cash flow figure suggests. Management Adjusted Free Cash Flow was CAD 484.9 million for nine months, built from add-backs including CAD 104.5 million of transaction costs and CAD 74.2 million of cash paid to the Founder and CEO, plus CAD 182.4 million of incremental growth investments. Unadjusted operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment was CAD 37.3 million. Cash interest rose to CAD 172.5 million in Q3 2026 from CAD 118.1 million a year earlier. [CP-1]

5. The debt stack is long-dated but large. Maturities begin in 2028 (CAD 2,128.2 million of notes), then 2029 (CAD 1,844.4 million), the revolver in 2030 (CAD 868.0 million drawn) and 2031 onward; there is almost no current maturity (CAD 14.2 million). The Term Loan B and revolver are secured, the 6.750% 2031 notes no longer have collateral, and the notes' guarantor and ranking terms are not supplied. [CP-1 debt table]

6. Fixed commitments and structurally senior-type claims grew. Closure and post-closure obligations reached CAD 1,503.8 million, performance bonds CAD 2,324.1 million, letters of credit CAD 535.1 million and new crude oil transportation commitments CAD 561.4 million from the SECURE addition. These rank with operating claims and shape loss-given-default mechanics without giving an expected recovery outcome. [CP-1; CP-1A]

7. Control and event risk is live. A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals with a November 9, 2026 deadline, after the cutoff. A leveraged transaction could change financial policy and may engage change-of-control terms in debt documents that are not supplied. No outcome is assumed. [CP-1A]

8. Earnings quality is mixed. Net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million for nine months, driven by items outside Adjusted EBITDA (foreign exchange, financing costs, equity-method losses), and Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based payments (CAD 87.0 million) and transaction costs. Several guided figures imply an unusually small Q4 step (see Calculations), which is unverified. [CP-1; CP-1 calculations]

runs.text: Strengths. First, the business is recurring and vertically integrated: collection is the largest revenue line and landfill and transfer add disposal control, which supports revenue visibility and margin resilience (Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model). Second, earnings momentum is real in the filed figures: Adjusted EBITDA grew in each quarter of 2026 and management raised guidance three times, though guidance is Management Language. Third, the acquisition was paid mainly with equity, issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares, which limits the debt added by SECURE and leaves the revolver largely undrawn on a nominal basis relative to its size (the availability figure is not supplied). Fourth, the maturity profile has no material maturity before 2028 and interest on most notes is fixed in USD, with cross-currency swaps on the newest instruments (Documentary Fact). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact), and disclosure of non-IFRS bridges is detailed each quarter (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. First, leverage on reported earnings is high and rests on run-rate estimates for the stated ratio, so the margin for error against a 5.00x covenant depends on an unsupplied definition (Analyst Interpretation). Second, cash conversion after capital spending and interest is thin and management free cash flow relies on add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Third, integration risk: provisional purchase accounting, a large goodwill balance (CAD 12,583.1 million, versus CAD 6,894.9 million at December 31, 2025) and a net loss from continuing operations mean book equity is largely acquired intangibles (Documentary Fact). Fourth, the take-private review and a dual-class structure with unspecified voting terms leave control and future leverage policy uncertain (Insufficient Information on voting rights). Fifth, commodity and fuel exposure: diesel is cited as a margin headwind, and the new crude oil commitments add a fixed obligation whose counterparties and tenor are not supplied (Management Language; Documentary Fact). Sixth, foreign exchange: most notes are USD while much revenue is CAD and USD, a mix that moves reported leverage and caused a CAD 196.7 million foreign exchange loss in nine months (Documentary Fact).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The dominant transaction is the SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquisition. The definitive agreement was entered "On April 12, 2026" (Q1 statements note 18, subsequent events); SECURE shareholders approved it in May and it went through regulatory review (Q2 release); GFL acquired 100% of the common shares "On September 1, 2026" (Q3 statements note 3, page:7). Documentary Fact: total consideration of about 5,414.1 satisfied by share capital of 4,334.8 and cash of 1,079.3; SECURE operates waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling in Western Canada and North Dakota; initial accounting is provisional and based on historical carrying values, so fair value adjustments could change goodwill, intangibles, property and the 1,006.6 of other long-term liabilities assumed. Mechanism: issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares funded most of the price with equity, which limits the incremental debt, while the cash portion, repayment of acquired debt (if any, not stated in the supplied text) and transaction costs were funded with new debt. Credit implication: the equity-heavy structure moderates leverage growth, but the assumed obligations, closure liabilities of 271.8 and crude oil commitments broaden the senior and structurally senior claims ahead of or alongside the notes.

Alongside SECURE, GFL completed 13 businesses in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, each individually immaterial except SECURE, with combined purchase consideration for the others of 1,598.5 including 156.3 in shares (Q3 statements page:6). Management states year-to-date completed acquisitions generate "approximately $2 billion in annualized revenue" (Q3 release page:1) which is Management Language, not a filed fact.

New financing during 2026 (Documentary Fact, Q3 statements page:11 to page:14): a Term Loan B Facility entered August 28, 2026 maturing August 28, 2033 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at 1,418.8; 5.500% senior notes due February 1, 2034 (1,418.8) and 5.625% senior notes due July 1, 2031 (1,064.1), the latter with a cross-currency swap fixing the rate at 4.480% (entered June 25, 2026); a swap on the Term Loan B fixing the rate at 5.009%; the revolving credit agreement amended and restated through September 1, 2026 maturing April 29, 2030. The issuance of debt in the nine months was 6,795.9 and repayment 3,823.9 (cash flow statement, page:4). The use of proceeds is not stated in the supplied text beyond the statement that financing and acquisition activity occurred; the sources and uses of the SECURE financing are therefore partly Insufficient Information. The 6.750% 2031 notes had their collateral released and are no longer secured (note 7), which is a Documentary Fact bearing on the secured-unsecured balance of the capital structure; the indenture terms that permitted the release are not supplied.

Pending event, after the cutoff in resolution: in the third quarter a Special Committee of independent directors was formed to review unsolicited proposals to take the Company private, with updated proposals due November 9, 2026 (Q3 release page:1). Management Language states "There can be no assurance that the Company will receive any proposals". A take-private would raise change-of-control, leveraged buyout and covenant questions; indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity cannot be assessed. No outcome may be assumed.

Subsequent events: after March 31, 2026 GFL completed 5 acquisitions for about 1,437.6 (Q1 statements note 18); that disclosure was dated to the Q1 period and is not folded into Q1 figures. The Q3 statements contain no subsequent-events note in the extracted text.

fields.value: The dominant transaction is the SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquisition. The definitive agreement was entered "On April 12, 2026" (Q1 statements note 18, subsequent events); SECURE shareholders approved it in May and it went through regulatory review (Q2 release); GFL acquired 100% of the common shares "On September 1, 2026" (Q3 statements note 3, page:7). Documentary Fact: total consideration of about 5,414.1 satisfied by share capital of 4,334.8 and cash of 1,079.3; SECURE operates waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling in Western Canada and North Dakota; initial accounting is provisional and based on historical carrying values, so fair value adjustments could change goodwill, intangibles, property and the 1,006.6 of other long-term liabilities assumed. Mechanism: issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares funded most of the price with equity, which limits the incremental debt, while the cash portion, repayment of acquired debt (if any, not stated in the supplied text) and transaction costs were funded with new debt. Credit implication: the equity-heavy structure moderates leverage growth, but the assumed obligations, closure liabilities of 271.8 and crude oil commitments broaden the senior and structurally senior claims ahead of or alongside the notes.

fields.value: Alongside SECURE, GFL completed 13 businesses in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, each individually immaterial except SECURE, with combined purchase consideration for the others of 1,598.5 including 156.3 in shares (Q3 statements page:6). Management states year-to-date completed acquisitions generate "approximately $2 billion in annualized revenue" (Q3 release page:1) which is Management Language, not a filed fact.

fields.value: New financing during 2026 (Documentary Fact, Q3 statements page:11 to page:14): a Term Loan B Facility entered August 28, 2026 maturing August 28, 2033 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at 1,418.8; 5.500% senior notes due February 1, 2034 (1,418.8) and 5.625% senior notes due July 1, 2031 (1,064.1), the latter with a cross-currency swap fixing the rate at 4.480% (entered June 25, 2026); a swap on the Term Loan B fixing the rate at 5.009%; the revolving credit agreement amended and restated through September 1, 2026 maturing April 29, 2030. The issuance of debt in the nine months was 6,795.9 and repayment 3,823.9 (cash flow statement, page:4). The use of proceeds is not stated in the supplied text beyond the statement that financing and acquisition activity occurred; the sources and uses of the SECURE financing are therefore partly Insufficient Information. The 6.750% 2031 notes had their collateral released and are no longer secured (note 7), which is a Documentary Fact bearing on the secured-unsecured balance of the capital structure; the indenture terms that permitted the release are not supplied.

fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: collection is the largest service line and pricing is described as "5.7% from core pricing" (Q3 release page:2). Mechanism: route-based collection revenue with pricing above inflation supports revenue visibility and margin resilience, while landfill and transfer volumes depend on construction and industrial activity. Implication: stable operating cash generation supports debt service tolerance, subject to the pricing claim being management's and to customer contract data being absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Leverage and acquisition integration. Evidence: Net Leverage 3.8x against 3.4x at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 handoff), and an unadjusted net-debt-to-trailing-Adjusted-EBITDA calculation above 5x in CP-1. Mechanism: SECURE contributes one month of EBITDA but all of its debt-funded cost and assumed liabilities, so reported coverage and leverage understate or overstate depending on whether run-rate adjustments of 730.9 are realised. Implication: refinancing and covenant headroom depend on the Material Acquisition step-up and on delivery of run-rate earnings; monitoring posture should be heightened until two full quarters including SECURE are reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Control and take-private uncertainty. Evidence: Special Committee and November 9, 2026 deadline (Q3 release page:1). Mechanism: a leveraged buyout or sponsor takeover could add debt or trigger change-of-control provisions in notes and credit facilities. Implication: monitoring item; no conclusion without indentures and credit agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Cash-flow conversion. Evidence: management Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 484.9 for nine months against unadjusted operating cash flow less capex of 37.3 (CP-1 calculation). Mechanism: large add-backs (transaction costs, CEO remuneration, incremental growth investments) bridge the two. Implication: the committee should read management free cash flow alongside the unadjusted figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Structural claims. Evidence: closure obligations, performance bonds and letters of credit (Q3 statements page:11, page:18, page:19). Mechanism: asset retirement and surety obligations rank with operating claims and rise with landfill acquisitions. Implication: recovery prospects for unsecured noteholders depend on asset coverage after secured facilities and these obligations; no expected recovery outcome is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: GFL Environmental Inc. is a resilient, price-led waste operator whose credit profile has weakened in the near term because the SECURE acquisition lifted carrying debt by CAD 4,248.8 million in nine months and management Net Leverage to 3.8x from 3.4x. The strongest support is steady collection and landfill earnings, with Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 678.7 million, a 31.5% margin, stated covenant compliance and mostly equity-funded purchase consideration. The weakest point is thin unadjusted cash generation: operating cash flow less capital spending was CAD 37.3 million over nine months, and net debt is 5.05x trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA. The outcome depends on SECURE earnings reaching the run-rate management assumes, headroom under the 5.00x acquisition covenant step-up, and the take-private review. The pack cannot confirm any of the three.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Confidence: Medium for the business view (Documentary Fact and Management Language mix); Low for forward leverage and covenant headroom (Insufficient Information on covenant values, run-rate bridge and liquidity).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. GFL Environmental Inc. changed perimeter on September 1, 2026. SECURE was bought for about CAD 5,414.1 million, of which CAD 4,334.8 million was shares and CAD 1,079.3 million cash, but only one month of SECURE earnings is in the Q3 2026 statements. Reported leverage measures therefore carry the full debt and assumed liabilities against a partial earnings base. [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Leverage depends on management estimates. Net Leverage of 3.8x divides CAD 11,399.9 million of net debt by Run-Rate EBITDA of CAD 2,988.0 million, of which CAD 730.9 million (about a quarter) is management adjustment; on trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 2,257.1 million the same net debt is 5.05x. The covenant ceiling is 5.00x for four fiscal quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom cannot be measured. Management guides to Net Leverage "in the mid 3s" by the end of 2026, a forward claim. [CP-1 calculations]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Operating performance is solid by management's account. Revenue grew 27.2% in Q3 2026, Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.8%, and the quarterly Adjusted EBITDA sequence of CAD 478.5, 591.2 and 678.7 million shows growth through the year, with core pricing near 6% stated by management. The reported margin was 31.5% against 31.6% a year earlier, so margin expansion exists only in management's underlying measure, which excludes M&A and diesel effects. [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Cash generation is weaker than the management free cash flow figure suggests. Management Adjusted Free Cash Flow was CAD 484.9 million for nine months, built from add-backs including CAD 104.5 million of transaction costs and CAD 74.2 million of cash paid to the Founder and CEO, plus CAD 182.4 million of incremental growth investments. Unadjusted operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment was CAD 37.3 million. Cash interest rose to CAD 172.5 million in Q3 2026 from CAD 118.1 million a year earlier. [CP-1]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. The debt stack is long-dated but large. Maturities begin in 2028 (CAD 2,128.2 million of notes), then 2029 (CAD 1,844.4 million), the revolver in 2030 (CAD 868.0 million drawn) and 2031 onward; there is almost no current maturity (CAD 14.2 million). The Term Loan B and revolver are secured, the 6.750% 2031 notes no longer have collateral, and the notes' guarantor and ranking terms are not supplied. [CP-1 debt table]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Fixed commitments and structurally senior-type claims grew. Closure and post-closure obligations reached CAD 1,503.8 million, performance bonds CAD 2,324.1 million, letters of credit CAD 535.1 million and new crude oil transportation commitments CAD 561.4 million from the SECURE addition. These rank with operating claims and shape loss-given-default mechanics without giving an expected recovery outcome. [CP-1; CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Control and event risk is live. A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals with a November 9, 2026 deadline, after the cutoff. A leveraged transaction could change financial policy and may engage change-of-control terms in debt documents that are not supplied. No outcome is assumed. [CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Earnings quality is mixed. Net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million for nine months, driven by items outside Adjusted EBITDA (foreign exchange, financing costs, equity-method losses), and Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based payments (CAD 87.0 million) and transaction costs. Several guided figures imply an unusually small Q4 step (see Calculations), which is unverified. [CP-1; CP-1 calculations]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, the business is recurring and vertically integrated: collection is the largest revenue line and landfill and transfer add disposal control, which supports revenue visibility and margin resilience (Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model). Second, earnings momentum is real in the filed figures: Adjusted EBITDA grew in each quarter of 2026 and management raised guidance three times, though guidance is Management Language. Third, the acquisition was paid mainly with equity, issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares, which limits the debt added by SECURE and leaves the revolver largely undrawn on a nominal basis relative to its size (the availability figure is not supplied). Fourth, the maturity profile has no material maturity before 2028 and interest on most notes is fixed in USD, with cross-currency swaps on the newest instruments (Documentary Fact). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact), and disclosure of non-IFRS bridges is detailed each quarter (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, leverage on reported earnings is high and rests on run-rate estimates for the stated ratio, so the margin for error against a 5.00x covenant depends on an unsupplied definition (Analyst Interpretation). Second, cash conversion after capital spending and interest is thin and management free cash flow relies on add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Third, integration risk: provisional purchase accounting, a large goodwill balance (CAD 12,583.1 million, versus CAD 6,894.9 million at December 31, 2025) and a net loss from continuing operations mean book equity is largely acquired intangibles (Documentary Fact). Fourth, the take-private review and a dual-class structure with unspecified voting terms leave control and future leverage policy uncertain (Insufficient Information on voting rights). Fifth, commodity and fuel exposure: diesel is cited as a margin headwind, and the new crude oil commitments add a fixed obligation whose counterparties and tenor are not supplied (Management Language; Documentary Fact). Sixth, foreign exchange: most notes are USD while much revenue is CAD and USD, a mix that moves reported leverage and caused a CAD 196.7 million foreign exchange loss in nine months (Documentary Fact).
